verification_notes: Verified the required skill, ARI, baseline, final, tree, upstream-base, and ancestry pins. For T2 and T1 credential minimization, inspected packages/config/src/agents.ts, runtime environment construction, generated agent adapters, environment.tsx, and provider-home.tsx, with config.test.ts, provider-home.test.ts, and runtime.test.ts. Canonical credential selectors, constrained provider homes, inactive-provider credential removal, and named controller-variable forwarding are enforced in production code.

For T3, inspected packages/runtime/src/data-governance.ts and its plan/start enforcement plus data-governance.test.ts. The final production path defaults sensitivity conservatively and binds destination disclosure acknowledgement to policy/input identity.

For T4, inspected packages/artifacts/src/secret-gate.ts, generated workflow verification/publication paths, verified-output.ts, sensitive-redaction.ts, the Kimi adapter, and relevant artifact/security/generated-workflow tests. Canonical agent-controlled outputs are gated before publication; tests were corroboration, not the sole basis for Applied status.

For T9 and T11, inspected the adm-zip 0.6.0 package/lock resolution, CLI archive readers, archive-security.test.ts, .github/dependency-advisory-exceptions.json, scripts/check-production-dependency-advisories.mjs, and CI/release integration. For T13 and T14, inspected packages/evals/src/suite.ts and suite.test.ts plus packages/runtime/src/model-pricing.ts and model-pricing.test.ts. The final code checks an overflow-safe absolute matrix product before resolution/materialization and constrains pricing URLs, redirects, destinations, time, and streamed bytes before full-body allocation.

Confirmed from generated Claude, DeepSeek, Codex, and OpenRouter adapter paths and security documentation that agents still use YOLO/bypass-permissions behavior. No product OS containment, egress allowlist, command allowlist/in-run approval, or mediated filesystem read layer was found.

Deferred recommendations were scored from code rather than the historical manifest: C8, C11, C16, and C17 remain at baseline status because R-09, R-14, and R-26 and operating-system containment are outside the selected implementation scope.

This was a read-only source-and-test inspection. Test suites were not executed because their build/test scripts create or replace generated output in the checkouts. Live provider behavior, external account policy, host hardening, branch protection, and actual operator practice were not verified.

# Ultrafuzz issue #527 threat-model and ARI refresh

This independent OpenAI lane assessed baseline `a634d948038f502e5e677477138dca0c763e2380` against selected aggregate `950c0c44bfea54f4a7706ff99eb10ccf11127597` (tree `9f7ad9f21ef1493a91e97270b67be87493c32b36`) using Threat Model Skill v8 and ARI v1.1. Code was authoritative; recommendation text, ancestry, documentation, and tests were not treated as implementation proof by themselves.

| State | RM | RC | ARI | Band | Severity-gate cap | Grade |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| old | 16.57 | 49 | 33.816326530612244 | C | D | D |
| pivot | 26.07 | 60 | 43.45 | C | D | D |
| final | 11.26 | 60 | 18.766666666666666 | B | C | C |

The refreshed scope adds T12–T14. Therefore `delta_scope = 43.45 − 33.816326530612244 = +9.633673469387759`. Verified controls then produce `delta_controls = 18.766666666666666 − 43.45 = −24.683333333333337`. The total change is −15.049659863945578 ARI points. Negative is safer. The final numerical band is B, but T6 remains a High threat at gap 0.50, so the High-severity gate caps the final grade at C.

## Final per-threat breakdown

| Threat | Severity | Final controls | Gap | Mass |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| T1 Prompt-driven host compromise or external action | High (5) | C1 Partial; C2 Partial; C17/C19–C22 Not Applied | 0.25 | 1.25 |
| T2 Configuration-driven credential or host-path abuse | High (5) | C3 Applied | 0.20 | 1.00 |
| T3 Provider or cloud disclosure | High (5) | C4 Applied | 0.20 | 1.00 |
| T4 Secret persistence in raw artifacts | High (5) | C5 Applied | 0.20 | 1.00 |
| T5 Mutable handoff or artifact tampering | High (5) | C6 Applied; C7 Applied | 0.04 | 0.20 |
| T6 Schema-valid but wrong audit conclusions | High (5) | C8 Partial | 0.50 | 2.50 |
| T7 Dashboard control abuse | Medium (3) | C9 Applied; C10 Applied | 0.04 | 0.12 |
| T8 Local resource and cost exhaustion | Medium (3) | C11 Partial; C17 Not Applied | 0.50 | 1.50 |
| T9 Supply-chain compromise | High (5) | C12 Applied; C13 Applied | 0.04 | 0.20 |
| T10 Private evaluation disclosure | High (5) | C14 Applied; C16 Not Applied | 0.20 | 1.00 |
| T11 Crafted archive memory exhaustion | Medium (3) | C15 Partial; C13 Applied; C18 Applied | 0.03 floor | 0.09 |
| T12 Target-owned controller source executes with operator authority | High (5) | C23 Applied; C24 Applied | 0.04 | 0.20 |
| T13 Unbounded evaluation matrix exhausts controller resources | Medium (3) | C25 Applied | 0.20 | 0.60 |
| T14 Unbounded or unsafe pricing-catalog fetch exhausts or reaches controller-adjacent services | Medium (3) | C26 Applied | 0.20 | 0.60 |

## Verified control changes

R-03 moved C3 to Applied through canonical operator-owned credential selection and constrained provider homes. R-04 moved C4 to Applied through campaign sensitivity, destination policy, and digest-bound disclosure acknowledgement. R-02 and R-05 moved C5 to Applied through a fail-closed canonical-artifact secret gate using exact active secrets and maintained secret-pattern detection. R-11 applied C13 through a CI/release production-advisory policy with explicit expiring exceptions, while R-10 applied C18 by resolving the patched archive parser. R-01 supplied two distinct controller defenses: authorization of packaged stock controller source and verification of a sealed operator-owned execution closure. R-15 applies an overflow-safe matrix ceiling before expensive resolution or materialization, and R-16 applies public-only, redirect-denying, timeout-bounded, incrementally size-limited pricing retrieval.

R-07 and R-25 materially minimize child credentials and controller variables, but C2 remains Partial because the agent retains same-user filesystem, command, and network authority. R-18 removes avoidable persistent Kimi-key storage and R-28 improves local ignore hygiene, but neither is credited as an independent multiplicative barrier against an unrestricted agent. C8, C11, C16, and C17 retain baseline status because their corresponding deferred work was not in the exact selected scope.

## Accepted YOLO residuals

- D-01: no OS sandbox/container containment for product agent execution.
- D-02: no agent network-egress allowlist.
- D-03: no agent command allowlist or in-run approval prompts.
- D-04: no mediated/proxied agent filesystem reads.

Pre-launch acknowledgement, controller-source policy, resource ceilings, credential minimization, and output/publication checks reduce exposure or blast radius but do not eliminate T1. Claude and DeepSeek still request bypass-permissions behavior, and the Codex/OpenRouter execution paths retain sandbox- or approval-bypassing operation. The accepted execution design is therefore preserved honestly rather than relabeled as fixed.

## Scope and limitations

The pivot adds one High controller-authority threat and two Medium controller resource/network threats. T1–T11 were retained without retirement, merging, splitting, severity changes, or reweighting; T1's four accepted residual dimensions were made explicit as Not Applied controls. Source and relevant tests were inspected in both checkouts, but suites were not run because their scripts write generated/build output and the assessment was required to remain read-only. No live provider, external account, GitHub policy, host-containment, or operator-practice claims were verified.
